material: One batch of Aalborg Portland white cement and water
preparation: Water added to cement; mixed at 1600 rpm for 120 s. EMM-ARM moulds vibrated to remove air; monitoring began within 20 min. Moist sealed curing.
recipe_basis: Measured water/cement ratios, expressed per 1 kg dry cement; not kg per cubic metre

heat_flow.unit: W/kg dry cement (numerically equal to the plotted mW/g)
heat_flow.method: Isothermal TAM Air calorimetry at 20 C

modulus.method: EMM-ARM low-frequency flexural resonance; not an ultrasound modulus or a direct compression test
modulus.replicates: Two runs per paste; the published figure contains one representative curve per recipe, not separate replicate records

extraction: Published PDF vector paths; line vertices retained and cubic Bezier segments sampled in 16 subdivisions; axes calibrated from their tick marks. W32/W40 initial heat-flow spikes double back horizontally in the artwork: extraction starts at the subsequent single-valued part. The W32 modulus segment crossing the zero-age tick is clipped at that tick by interpolation. These are figure-derived values, not raw instrument records or extra replicates. Rebuild with scripts/prepare_paste_benchmark.py (requires PyMuPDF).
reaction_coordinate: Heat increment per kg dry cement since the earliest common age supported by both figures for all three recipes. The unknown earlier heat is not set to zero total hydration.
heat_normalization: No absolute degree of hydration is inferred: the accepted manuscript gives 558 J/g in equation (4) on PDF p15 and 588 J/g in section 4.1 on p17.
temperature_dependence: These three recipes were measured at 20 C only. Granja et al. (2023), doi:10.3151/jact.21.803, provides a separate CEM I 52.5N, w/c=0.54 temperature benchmark; it is not a measurement of the W32/W40/W48 activation energy.
volumetric_properties: Fresh density, air fraction, conductivity and heat capacity are not assigned by this data product. Cement mass fraction is computed directly from the measured recipe; volume-based dosage needs a separate density basis.
application: Public cement-paste material benchmark for the support-calculation method.
